node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Vector components

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Vector magnitude and direction
node.description: Calculate and interpret vector magnitude and direction from components or diagrams.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Vector addition and subtraction
node.description: Add and subtract vectors geometrically and algebraically using components.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Scalar multiplication of vectors
node.description: Multiply vectors by scalars and interpret changes to magnitude and direction.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Unit vectors
node.description: Use unit vectors to represent directions and normalise vectors.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Position and displacement vectors

node.description: Calculate dot products and connect them to magnitudes, angles and perpendicularity.

node.label: Matrix multiplication

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Components encode displacement
node.description: Vector components describe signed horizontal and vertical displacement.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Magnitude is vector length
node.description: A vector's magnitude is its length or size, independent of its starting position.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Dot product detects perpendicularity
node.description: A zero dot product indicates perpendicular non-zero vectors.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Matrix dimensions control operations
node.description: Matrix dimensions determine whether addition or multiplication is defined and what size the result has.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Identity matrix leaves matrices unchanged
node.description: Multiplying by a compatible identity matrix leaves a matrix or vector unchanged.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Zero determinant means no inverse
node.description: A two-by-two matrix with determinant zero has no inverse.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Matrix product order matters
node.description: Matrix multiplication is generally not commutative, so the order of multiplication matters.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Vector treated as point only
node.description: Learner treats a vector only as a fixed point rather than a directed displacement with magnitude and direction.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Magnitude keeps component signs
node.description: Learner gives a signed component or coordinate as the magnitude rather than a non-negative length.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Matrix multiplication as entrywise multiplication
node.description: Learner multiplies corresponding entries instead of using row-by-column products for matrix multiplication.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Assume matrix multiplication is commutative
node.description: Learner assumes AB equals BA for matrices whenever both products are defined.

edge.rationale: Vector components are foundational to algebraic vector operations.
Magnitude and direction are core vector properties.
Vector addition and subtraction are core vector operations.
Scalar multiplication is a core vector operation affecting length and direction.
Dot products extend vector operations to angle and projection reasoning.
Matrix dimensions are foundational to matrix operations.
Matrix addition and scalar multiplication are basic operations.
Matrix multiplication is a central matrix operation.
Inverse matrices support solving matrix equations and systems.
Matrix transformations are a core application of matrix multiplication.
Vector components are coordinate displacements and require Cartesian coordinate understanding.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot interpret signed horizontal and vertical displacement.

edge.rationale: Magnitude and direction are calculated from components or diagrams.
edge.failure_signal: Learner confuses a signed component with the non-negative magnitude.

edge.rationale: Algebraic vector addition and subtraction combine corresponding components.
edge.failure_signal: Learner combines magnitudes rather than corresponding components.

edge.rationale: Scalar multiplication extends component operations by scaling every component.
edge.failure_signal: Learner scales only one component or misinterprets negative scalar direction reversal.

edge.rationale: Unit vectors require normalising a vector by its magnitude.
edge.failure_signal: Learner creates a vector with the wrong length or loses direction.

edge.rationale: Position and displacement vectors use coordinate components between points.
edge.failure_signal: Learner subtracts endpoints in the wrong order or treats positions and displacements as identical.

edge.rationale: Dot product connects component products with magnitudes and angles.
edge.failure_signal: Learner computes a vector result instead of a scalar or cannot connect dot product to angle.

edge.rationale: Vector projections use dot products to measure the component of one vector in another direction.
edge.failure_signal: Learner projects with the wrong direction vector or misses normalisation.

edge.rationale: Vector equations of lines use a starting position vector and a direction vector.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot distinguish a point on the line from a direction vector.

edge.rationale: Matrices use rectangular arrays; exact prerequisite path may vary by course sequence.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot interpret rows, columns and entries in a structured array.

edge.rationale: Matrix addition and scalar multiplication require interpreting dimensions and corresponding entries.
edge.failure_signal: Learner adds incompatible matrices or mismatches entries.

edge.rationale: Matrix multiplication depends on compatible dimensions and row-column structure.
edge.failure_signal: Learner multiplies corresponding entries or uses incompatible dimensions.

edge.rationale: Identity matrices are understood through their effect under matrix multiplication.
edge.failure_signal: Learner treats the identity matrix like a zero matrix or scalar one without dimension.

edge.rationale: Two-by-two determinants require identifying entries of a square matrix.
edge.failure_signal: Learner uses the wrong diagonal products or ignores matrix order.

edge.rationale: The inverse of a two-by-two matrix depends on a non-zero determinant.
edge.failure_signal: Learner tries to invert a matrix with zero determinant or misuses the inverse formula.

edge.rationale: Solving matrix equations with inverses requires knowing inverse matrices.
edge.failure_signal: Learner multiplies on the wrong side or misrepresents the system as a matrix equation.

edge.rationale: Matrix transformations apply matrix multiplication to coordinate vectors.
edge.failure_signal: Learner treats transformation matrices as coordinate points rather than operators.

edge.rationale: Composite matrix transformations apply successive transformations through matrix multiplication.
edge.failure_signal: Learner multiplies transformation matrices in the wrong order.
